terms.meaning: the markup language that defines a web page's structure
the container element where the React app draws its content
a script loaded in the modern way that supports importing other files

used_by: Browser when the app is opened

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Web page shell that loads the app
sections.what: This is the single web page the browser opens. It gives the page a title and a small icon, then leaves an empty spot with the id root where the app draws its screens. It also loads the main script, src/main.tsx.
sections.why: Likely reason: a React single-page app needs one host page that the script fills in at runtime.

summary: The single web page that loads the app. It sets the language, title, description, a small inline icon, and an empty root element where the app is drawn.
purpose: Gives the browser the starting page and tells it to load the frontend's main script.
why: Standard structure for a Vite and React app. Reason for the inline icon is not stated in the code.
how: The browser reads the page metadata, finds the root element, and then loads the main module script which draws the app inside that element.
inputs: No direct inputs. It depends on the built script at src/main.tsx.
outputs: The page shell that the app fills in.
risks: If the script path or the root element id changes, the app shows a blank page.
debug: If the page is blank, check that the root element id matches the app code, then check the browser console for script load errors.
